assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing turned DNA polymerase chemistry (reversible terminators, clonal clusters, single-molecule chemistry on surfaces) into the dominant readout of genomes. From my vantage in replication fidelity and nucleotide metabolism it is a chemical invention with enormous enabling effect across biology and medicine, and the underlying nucleotide-analogue and polymerase chemistry is concrete and well defined.
assessment.attribution: The Solexa chemistry of reversible-terminator sequencing-by-synthesis is most clearly traced to Balasubramanian and Klenerman. Rothberg (pyrosequencing-based emulsion-PCR platform), Ju and Mayer made distinct contributions to other platforms and clustering, so a two-person prize would leave out parallel routes; credit is separable but contested in breadth.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed and in universal use for about two decades; recognition is timely to overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as chemistry rather than biotechnology or physiology/medicine territory.
Allocation among Solexa, 454 and other platform inventors; I rely on recalled history, not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hijacking the ubiquitin-proteasome system with bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues (including the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide-class drugs) converts protein degradation into a chemically programmable event-driven pharmacology. It is a real mechanism-to-tool story, with a general design principle and clinical candidates, which I value as a biochemist.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept and first demonstrations; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target underlying molecular glues. Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and others made major later advances, so selection of three is defensible but leaves out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Concept validated by many independent groups and multiple clinical-stage degraders; approvals are still pending, which makes it slightly early but near-ready.
uncertainties: Clinical efficacy is not yet established by an approved PROTAC drug.
Division between PROTAC and molecular-glue lineages may need distinct recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalysed C-N coupling is a general, mechanistically understood transformation widely used in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. It is a prototypical chemistry prize case with high impact, clarity and long-standing independent validation.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general, ligand-controlled catalytic amination and clarified mechanism; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor, and the 2010 prize already recognised cross-coupling more broadly, so overlap is a concern.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature; the main question is overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize rather than evidence strength.
uncertainties: Committee may regard it as an extension of a recognised field.
Precedence of Kosugi versus the later catalytic generality.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles made nucleic-acid medicines deliverable in vivo and enabled siRNA therapy and mRNA vaccines at global scale. The advance is physical-organic lipid chemistry (pKa-tuned ionizable lipids, rapid-mixing formulation) with unambiguous, demonstrated impact.
assessment.attribution: The Vancouver group (Cullis, Madden, Hope) developed the core lipid-nanoparticle formulation and ionizable-lipid concept; MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer contributed lipid design and delivery systems. The chemistry-specific credit favours the Cullis group but the full allocation is not clean.
assessment.maturity: Clinically proven at scale by approved products; independent confirmation is overwhelming. The 2023 Medicine prize recognised the mRNA part, not the delivery chemistry.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Physiology or Medicine prize may affect perceived novelty.
Allocation among lipid-design versus formulation contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative, large-scale proteomics by mass spectrometry made it possible to measure proteins, modifications and interactions across whole cells. As someone who relies on LC-MS/MS quantification of small molecules, I appreciate the analytical rigour, and the effect on biology is broad.
assessment.attribution: Mann (high-resolution shotgun and quantitative proteomics), Aebersold (targeted and quantitative approaches) and Yates (database searching, MudPIT) are leading, but Hunt, Heck and Gygi also have claim, so the three-person limit forces difficult exclusions.
assessment.maturity: Mature and ubiquitous, but mass spectrometry for biomolecules was already recognised in 2002; incremental recognition may be debated.
uncertainties: Genuinely difficult credit division among six listed names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore reading of single DNA/RNA molecules is a new analytical principle that gave portable long-read sequencing and direct detection of modified nucleotides, including RNA modifications. It has high scientific and practical relevance to genome and nucleotide research.
assessment.attribution: Branton and Deamer proposed the concept, Kasianowicz demonstrated polynucleotide translocation, and Akeson and Bayley developed single-nucleotide discrimination with enzyme ratcheting. Credit is spread; my chosen trio is one reasonable choice, and I am not certain of the current status of all named individuals.
assessment.maturity: Commercially established with wide independent use, though accuracy and applications continue to evolve.
uncertainties: Uncertain whether all senior contributors are eligible.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reversible m6A methylation established an epitranscriptomic regulatory layer, with writers, erasers and readers and methods for mapping the modification. It is a chemical modification of RNA with clear biological effects and broad biomedical relevance.
assessment.attribution: He identified the FTO eraser function and reader proteins, Jaffrey and Rechavi (with Dominissini and Meyer) developed transcriptome-wide mapping; Jia, Yang and others contributed key early findings. Attribution is plausible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Strongly supported by many labs, though mechanisms of some functional claims, quantitation of stoichiometry and the physiological roles of individual marks are still debated and disputes persist.
uncertainties: Some functional claims have been challenged by quantitative measurements.
Medicine-oriented rather than chemistry-oriented framing is possible.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion with orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs allows site-specific incorporation of noncanonical amino acids into proteins in living cells, giving chemists a general tool to install new chemistry in biology.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the original orthogonal-pair strategy in vivo; Chin extended it to eukaryotes, multiple codes and quadruplet decoding. Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama contributed important systems.
assessment.maturity: Well reproduced and widely used as a tool; therapeutic and industrial applications are still emerging.
uncertainties: Breadth of downstream applications relative to the foundational tool.
